This report provides an update on a request for a horse drawn carriage business license to operate on city of Saskatoon streets and the ability to address these types of future one-off requests.
The current traffic bylaw does not permit horse drawn vehicles as they are classified as unregulated vehicles.
However, the general manager does have to discretion to issue permits to allow the registered owner or operator of an unregulated vehicle to operate within the city on designated routes.
Administration met with the applicant to revise the routes that were originally submitted in the application and is in the process of finalizing a temporary permit for the 2025-26 winter season.
Administration is working with the applicant to have the temporary permit issued before a year end.
The temporary permit will act as a pilot project to assess feasibility and impacts.
Indicators' success for the pilot are being finalized but is identified in the letter submitted by the applicant to council today.

They could include such things as reported safety incidences and concerns, compliance with the permit conditions, community and business concerns, and a final report back to committee on the findings of the pilot.
Administration will share the indicators of success of the pilot with the applicant when they've been fully developed.

Administration will also report back to the Standing Policy Committee of Transportation by Q3 of 2026 with the pilot findings including a jurisdictional scan and recommendations for licensing options for horse drawn carriage type services on city streets.
And a final note and administration would like to acknowledge this request should have been responded to in a timely or manner and apologize to the applicant for the delay.
We appreciate the applicant meeting with the administration to work through on a solution to position for the temporary permit to allow operations to commence as a pilot this winter season.
Lessons have been learned and a process for handling future one-off request is being developed to report back to committee by June of 2026.
